seoTitle: How to Cancel a Domain and Get a Refund on GoDaddy
metaDescription: Learn how to cancel a GoDaddy domain properly, check refund eligibility, turn off auto-renewal, and request a refund through live chat support.
intro: Buying a domain by mistake, or realizing you no longer need one, is common enough that GoDaddy has a defined refund process for it — but the process only works if you follow it in the right order. Cancel or let the domain expire without checking the policy first, and you can lose the refund window; leave auto-renewal on while you sort out the cancellation, and you can get charged again before anything is resolved. This guide walks through checking GoDaddy's refund terms, turning off auto-renewal, and requesting the refund itself through GoDaddy's live chat support, using the same domain portfolio and chat screens you'll actually see in your own account.

steps.heading: Find the domain in your account
steps.body: Log in to GoDaddy and open your Domain Portfolio, then select the specific domain you want to cancel. This opens the domain's own overview page, which is also where you'll do most of the rest of the work in this guide — renewal settings, DNS, and account details for that one domain all live here rather than in a general settings menu.

steps.heading: Read the refund policy before you do anything else
steps.body: GoDaddy's refund terms are specific and time-boxed: annual plans are generally refundable within 30 days (720 hours) of the transaction, while monthly plans have a much tighter 48-hour window. Some products carry their own special terms on top of that — ad spend, assisted services, and auction listings each have different rules, so don't assume the standard 30-day window applies to everything on your account. Check this page for your specific product before you cancel, since canceling first and asking about a refund second can put you outside the eligible window by the time you actually make the request.

image.caption: GoDaddy's refund terms, showing the 30-day window for annual plans and the shorter 48-hour window for monthly plans.

steps.heading: Turn off auto-renewal on the domain
steps.body: On the domain's Overview tab, the Renew panel shows the Auto-renew toggle along with the expiration date and renewal cost. Switch auto-renewal off here regardless of whether you're also canceling or requesting a refund — it's the one setting that stops a surprise charge from hitting your card while everything else is still in progress. This is a per-domain setting, so if you're cleaning up more than one unwanted domain, you'll need to repeat this step on each one individually.

image.caption: The domain's Overview tab, with Auto-renew switched off and the expiration date and yearly renewal cost shown alongside it.

steps.heading: Cancel the domain rather than expecting a straight deletion
steps.body: It's worth knowing going in that GoDaddy doesn't offer a literal "delete this domain" button — a domain registration is canceled or left to expire, not removed outright, because the registration itself is tied to ICANN records rather than just your account. Practically, this means the option you're looking for in your account is a cancellation flow, not a delete option, and asking support for a "deletion" will usually just get redirected into the cancellation-and-refund conversation anyway.

steps.heading: Request the refund through live chat
steps.body: GoDaddy's Help Center has a Chat Now option that opens an AI assistant first, which asks what you need before connecting you to a human Guide. Stating your request plainly — for example, that you want to cancel the domain and get a refund — moves things along fastest, since the assistant's job at that stage is mainly to route you to the right person rather than resolve the refund itself. Once it hands off, a Guide picks up the same conversation thread and can process the actual cancellation and refund request against your account.

image.caption: GoDaddy's live chat, with a refund request typed to the AI assistant before it hands the conversation off to a support Guide.

steps.heading: Confirm the outcome after you submit the request
steps.body: Once a Guide takes over, they'll confirm whether your purchase falls inside the refund window and process it if it does — refund timing back to your original payment method can still take several business days even after it's approved, so don't expect it to reflect immediately. Keep an eye on your email for GoDaddy's confirmation of both the cancellation and the refund, and double-check the domain's status in your portfolio afterward to make sure it's actually been canceled rather than just flagged for review.

faq.question: Is every domain purchase on GoDaddy refundable?
faq.answer: No — refund eligibility depends on the product and how recently you bought it. Annual plans are generally refundable within 30 days, monthly plans within 48 hours, and some products like ad spend or assisted services follow different rules entirely, so check GoDaddy's refund policy page for your specific purchase.

faq.question: How do I stop GoDaddy from renewing a domain I don't want?
faq.answer: Open the domain in your Domain Portfolio and switch off Auto-renew on its Overview tab. Do this in addition to requesting cancellation, since turning off auto-renewal and canceling the domain are two separate actions.

faq.question: Can I delete a GoDaddy domain outright?
faq.answer: Not directly — GoDaddy's support confirms domains can't be deleted, only canceled or allowed to expire, because the registration is tied to ICANN records rather than just your account.

faq.question: Who do I contact for a GoDaddy refund?
faq.answer: Use GoDaddy's Help Center Chat Now option. It opens with an AI assistant that asks what you need, then hands you off to a human support Guide who can process the actual cancellation and refund.

faq.question: How long does a GoDaddy refund take to process?
faq.answer: Even after a Guide approves your refund, it can take several business days to reflect on your original payment method — confirm the expected timeline with support when you submit the request.
